facts.text: Perseverance Valley was deployed at Meridiani Planum during Opportunity (MER-B) in 2017.

Opportunity's final resting place is in Perseverance Valley, a shallow channel carved into the western rim of Endeavour Crater. The rover was studying how the valley formed — by water, wind, or ice — when the 2018 global dust storm ended its mission. The valley was named for the rover's remarkable longevity.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
A shallow channel whose origin — water, wind, or ice — was under active investigation when the mission ended; its formation mechanism remains an open question.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Meridiani Planum.
Perseverance Valley is Opportunity's final resting place; the rover sits partway down the channel, forever mid-investigation.
